ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus. Points E and F are located on sides BC and CD, respectively, with BE = DF and AB = AE. If $\angle EAF=75^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
it follows that AB = AD, $\angle B$ = $\angle D$, and $\angle C$ = $\angle BAD$. \\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle ADF$, \\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l} AB = AD \\ \angle B = \angle D \\ BE = DF \end{array}\right.$, \\
it implies that $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle ADF$ (SAS), \\
thus, $\angle DAF = \angle BAE$. \\
Let $\angle BAE = \angle DAF = x$, \\
then $\angle DAE = 75^\circ + x$, \\
and since AD $\parallel$ BC, \\
$\angle AEB = 75^\circ + x$. \\
Given that AB = AE, \\
$\angle B = \angle AEB = 75^\circ + x$. \\
Since $\angle BAE + \angle ABE + \angle AEB = 180^\circ$, \\
$x + 75^\circ + x + 75^\circ + x = 180^\circ$, \\
thus $x = 10^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BAD = 95^\circ$, \\
which means $\angle C = \boxed{95^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus. Points E and F are on sides BC and CD, respectively, with BE = DF and AB = AE. If \angle EAF = 75^\circ, what is the measure of \angle C?
raw_record.answer: Given that ABCD is a rhombus, AB = AD, \angle B = \angle D, and \angle C = \angle BAD. In triangles ABE and ADF, AB = AD, \angle B = \angle D, and BE = DF, so \triangle ABE \cong \triangle ADF (SAS), hence \angle DAF = \angle BAE. Let \angle BAE = \angle DAF = x. Then \angle DAE = 75^\circ + x. Since AD \parallel BC, \angle AEB = 75^\circ + x. Given AB = AE, \angle B = \angle AEB = 75^\circ + x. From triangle ABE: x + (75^\circ + x) + (75^\circ + x) = 180^\circ, so x = 10^\circ. Therefore \angle BAD = 95^\circ, and \angle C = 95^\circ.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, with A above, C below, B on the left side, and D on the right side; E is located on side BC, and F is located on side CD; from A, line segments are respectively connected to E and F, and the angle given in the figure that is required to be used is ∠EAF. Reasoning: ABCD is a rhombus, so AB = AD, ∠B = ∠D, and opposite angles are equal, ∠C = ∠BAD. Because E is on BC and F is on CD, in △ABE and △ADF, AB = AD, BE = DF, and the included angle ∠ABE = ∠ADF, therefore △ABE ≅ △ADF (SAS). Thus ∠BAE = ∠DAF. Let ∠BAE = ∠DAF = x. It is known that ∠EAF = 75°, so ∠BAD = x + 75° + x = 75° + 2x. Also ∠DAE = ∠DAF + ∠FAE = x + 75°. Because AD ∥ BC, and E is on BC, ∠AEB = ∠DAE = 75° + x. It is known that AB = AE, therefore △ABE is an isosceles triangle, ∠ABE = ∠AEB = 75° + x. In △ABE, x + (75° + x) + (75° + x) = 180°, that is, 3x + 150° = 180°, solving gives x = 10°. So ∠BAD = 75° + 2×10° = 95°. Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, therefore ∠C = ∠BAD = 95°.
